newsitem.title: USA: WellPoint Health buying John Hancock group health units.
newsitem.headline: WellPoint Health buying John Hancock group health units.

text.p: WellPoint Health Networks Inc. said Friday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire the group health and related life insurance business of John Hancock Mutual Life Insurance Co. for $86.7 million.

The deal is the second such acquisition this year by WellPoint, one of the nation's largest publicly held managed health care companies. It purchased the group life and health business of Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance Co. earlier this year.

WellPoint, based in Woodland Hills, Calif., said the acquisition of the Hancock business, which currently provides services to an estimated 1.4 million members, will expand WellPoint's membership base to 5.5 million nationwide.

The acquisition also includes Hancock's managed care services subsidiary, Cost Care Inc., WellPoint said. The agreement does not include Hancock's group long-term care business or its unrelated stand-alone group life business.
WellPoint said it was purchasing the Hancock business as a separate unit and will offer positions to all 2,950 Hancock employees, including some 600 in the greater Boston area.

"This business unit will focus on very large national customers, merging WellPoint's creative managed care model with John Hancock's expertise in servicing these very demanding Fortune 500 customers," the company said.

WellPoint said Hancock's group life and health business, serving some of the largest employers in the nation, has a concentration of business in key geographic areas that are complementary to areas already served by WellPoint.
Nearly two-thirds of Hancock's members are located in California, Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Illinois, Michigan and Massachusetts and in the New York City and Washington, D.C., metropolitan areas.

"Strategically, gaining significant membership in targeted geographies creates the base to expand and diversify our innovative network models across the country," Chairman Leonard D. Schaeffer said in a statement. "This provides a platform for launching our individual, senior and small employer group businesses in these key markets."
Cost Care, Hancock's California-based managed care services subsidiary, serves more than 650 clients, providing services to more than 3 million individuals.

Hancock also has nearly 1 million members covered through group life and disability insurance products linked to health coverage, which when combined with WellPoint will result in more than 1.5 million life and disability members.
The acquisition also includes Hancock's estimated 1.3 million dental members, giving WellPoint about 2.8 million dental members -- creating one of the largest dental businesses in the country.
The company said the closing, which is subject to regulatory approvals, is expected to occur no later than Jan. 31.
WellPoint's stock gained 50 cents to $31.875 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
